directions.style: Medieval chiptune. 8-bit console sound playing early music: a square-wave lead that phrases like a recorder or a shawm, a plucked pulse-wave lute arpeggio, a triangle-wave drone like a hurdy-gurdy, noise-channel tabor drum and tambourine. Modal melody in Dorian or Mixolydian, an estampie or a galliard dance feel, a castle court, minstrels, a tournament. Crunchy retro chip timbres, no modern synth pads, no orchestra

Age-of-sail chiptune. 8-bit console sound playing a sea shanty and a hornpipe: a square-wave lead that phrases like a fife or a tin whistle, pulse-wave chords pumping like a concertina, a triangle-wave bass walking like a tuba, noise-channel snare and a wooden-sounding drum. 6/8 jig lilt or a brisk 2/4 hornpipe, a harbour, sailors hauling rope, tall ships. Crunchy retro chip timbres, no modern synth pads, no orchestra

Renaissance-fanfare chiptune. 8-bit console sound playing court music: square-wave trumpets in fanfare thirds, a pulse-wave harpsichord-like accompaniment, triangle-wave bass, noise-channel field drum rolls. A royal procession, heralds, banners, a cannon salute. Crunchy retro chip timbres, no modern synth pads, no orchestra

build.prompt: Instrumental only, no vocals, no singing, no lyrics. {style}. Background music for the build phase of a cheerful castle board game: the player stacks painted wooden wall pieces on a tile board, friendly and quick, sunlit toy fortress by the sea. Tempo: 108 BPM. Mood: calm, bouncy, curious, light. Arrangement: a steady loop of a catchy eight-bar melody with a second eight bars that answers it, a light counter-melody, no big build-up, no breakdown, no ending, constant energy so it loops. About 90 seconds long.

battle.prompt: Instrumental only, no vocals, no singing, no lyrics. {style}. Background music for the battle phase of a cheerful castle board game: toy cannons pop like a fairground shooting gallery, water splashes, ships tip over like toys, nothing grim. Tempo: 150 BPM. Mood: driving, exciting, playful, heroic. Arrangement: a field-drum march pattern throughout, a fanfare-like main theme in the lead, a running bass, a second section with more tension, back to the theme, no slow intro, no ending, constant energy so it loops. About 90 seconds long.
